newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Analysts says P&U report reassures market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Analysts says P&U report reassures market.

text.p: Swedish/U.S. drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn (P&U) on Thursday posted a nine month report that reassured the market after a surprise profit warning three weeks ago, analysts said.
P&U unnerved investors when it warned adverse currency moves could drag earnings down to about 44 cents a share in the third quarter, disappointing analysts who hoped for 55 cents.
As foreshadowed on Thursday the pharceutical company posted earnings of 44 cents a share, steady with the third quarter of 1995, and a 12 percent drop in earnings to $204 million.
P&U's share price climbed on the Stockholm bourse on the report, rising 3.3 percent or eight crowns to 251 crowns within 30 minutes of its release.
"It does appear there is nothing sinister and operations are moving along quite well," analyst Stephen Putnam from Kleinwort Benson told Reuters.
"There is nothing untowards in either foreign currency management or underlying business."
The share price was at 275.50 crowns before the profit warning but plummeted as low as 238 crowns in the following week.
In its report P&U said the weaker Japanese yen, stronger Swedish crown and Italian lira increased costs in dollar terms and wiped two percent off sales growth in the third quarter.
Net sales in the three months ending September 30 still rose two percent on a year ago, reaching $1.7 billion.
Analysts said there appeared nothing wrong with the company's operations, with new products showing positive signs of growth.

"There were some small areas of diappointment in older products but this was balanced by a better than expected performance in some new products," said one London-based analysts who requested anonymity.
He picked out newly launched cancer drug Camptosar as a particularly strong performer as well as erective dysfunction product caverjet and glaucoma product Xalatan.
"This gives a little bit of comfort to investors adn teh share price has shown this relief," the analyst said.
"So far we have been shown nothing at all to suggest P&U won't meet its goals."
P&U put out a list of targets when the company was formed a year ago by the merger of Sweden's Pharmacia with Upjohn of the U.S.

P&U's chief executive, John Zabriskie, acknowledged foreign exchange had a disappointing effect on earnings but stressed that the longterm merger goals, including to have a 25 percent operating margin by 1998, remained unchanged.
Zabriskie said the company was on line to achieve annual cost savings of $500 million by 1998 with 85 percent of that in effect next year.
Analyst Jan Dworsky from Fiba told Reuters that the market was relieved to see that the company's currency losses were a credible explanation for the profit warning.
"Their credibility was negatively affected by this warning," Dworsky said.
"It is this and also that some new products look encouraging that has helped the share price rise."
